items.title: Many languages, one common neural code
items.rationale: Freshest, highest-credibility cognition result (MIT McGovern, Nature): a multilingual AI model used to compare brain responses across speakers of 21 languages suggests meaning is represented the same way regardless of language.
items.excerpt: MIT McGovern (Nature): analyzing speakers of 21 languages with a multilingual AI model, the study finds the human brain may represent meaning in much the same way across languages. Note: brain-model alignment angle (deprioritized).

items.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
items.rationale: New method, concrete claim: MIT's SLIC training lets a small generative model design analog integrated circuits as well as or better than frontier LLMs, cutting cost of a hard engineering-design task.
items.excerpt: MIT SLIC training teaches a small generative model to design analog integrated circuits as well as or better than frontier LLMs. Engineering-design angle; may fit gadgets better.

items.title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium-oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
items.rationale: Primary-source materials result with hard numbers: ML picked a Ni-Co dual-atom catalyst steering Li-O2 batteries to a four-electron LiOH pathway, ~60,000 mAh/g capacity and 2,000+ stable cycles.
items.excerpt: Authors use machine learning to identify a Ni-Co dual-atom catalyst that promotes a four-electron LiOH pathway in Li-O2 batteries, reaching ~60,000 mAh/g capacity and over 2,000 stable cycles.

items.title: One in four students turn to AI for mental health support
items.rationale: Fresh psychology survey (Bath, JMIR Mental Health, n=2,020): about one in four UK students used generative AI for mental-health support in six months, most among those with very low well-being — a behavioral finding, not a clinical one.
items.excerpt: University of Bath (JMIR Mental Health): survey of 2,020 UK students finds about one in four used generative AI for mental-health support in six months, highest among those with very low well-being. Cross-sectional survey (attitude-survey caveat).

items.title: Neural networks that behave identically reveal hidden structural differences as they learn
items.rationale: NeurIPS 2026 oral (Technion): RNNs with identical behavior hide structural differences that surface only when learning a new task — and the paper proposes tests for the same effect in biological circuits.
items.excerpt: Technion (arXiv 2605.04115, NeurIPS 2026 oral): RNNs with identical behavior carry hidden structural differences that surface only when learning a new task and retain traces of past training; proposes tests for biological circuits.
